---
title: "Research"
---

My research lies at the intersection of **probability theory, random discrete structures, and statistical inference**. I am interested in how much information is needed to recover features of networks and other probabilistic models.

## Random graphs and network archaeology

I have studied root finding in growing random networks, including recursive directed acyclic graphs and Cooper–Frieze random networks. This work asks how to identify the origin of a network from its observed structure.

## Statistical inference and graphical models

A recent direction concerns **testing structural properties of trees** underlying graphical models using covariance queries. The objective is to estimate or test global properties efficiently without necessarily reconstructing the full graph.

## Sequential random models

I have also worked on subtractive random forests and models motivated by sequential recommendation systems, studying their long-term probabilistic behavior.

## Emerging interests: quantum error correction

I am developing interests in quantum error-correcting codes, decoding algorithms, and probabilistic and combinatorial methods relevant to quantum information.

For papers and preprints, see [Publications](publications.qmd).
